case.adverse_disturbance: For the final closure, place one supplied 1 mm card at the rim's marked right contact point; all outcome requirements still apply except seal contact continuity.
case.description: Design a removable joint for a 300 mm inspection hatch on a dry tabletop trough fixture. A technician must open it repeatedly while retaining the existing hatch, rim and seal. All dimensions and observations below are stipulated for this hypothetical fixture.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform the hatch or trough.
Keep the full marked inspection opening unobstructed when open.
Use no powered mechanism; loose components must remain recoverable.
The seal must show no new visible tears after testing.

known_parent_functions.function: A strap retains an object against separation.
known_parent_functions.operating_path: Tension travels through the strap between its attachments.
known_parent_functions.ordinary_use: Holding a parcel against a support during transport.

known_parent_functions.function: A spacer establishes a repeatable clearance.
known_parent_functions.operating_path: Its thickness limits how closely two surfaces approach.
known_parent_functions.ordinary_use: Setting a gap during fixture assembly.

observations: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.
probe_resources: Spring scale marked at 20 N, stopwatch, ruler, ten numbered cycle cards and two 1 mm cards.
Up to two alternative joint configurations and twelve total closure/pull trials, including at least one disturbed trial per configuration.
resources: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.
Ninety minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for observation.
case.valued_outcome: After ten opening cycles, the closed hatch stays within 1 mm of its marked position, withstands a supplied 20 N sideways pull, and can be reopened by one technician within 30 seconds.

openings.claim: Separating lateral location from seal compression with removable padded strip stops could resist sliding without the corner preload that lifts the opposite corner.
openings.delta: Allocate strips to lateral bearing and use only balanced seating pressure; accommodate the right-side card instead of tightening a corner to restore seal continuity.
openings.prediction: If the rim permits secure removable stop engagement, the hatch will remain within 1 mm under 20 N after ten openings, including disturbed final closure, without new seal tears.
openings.probe: Check removable rim engagement first. Hand-fabricate only supplied strips; measure position and corner lift through repeated closures and the final right-card closure. Inspect seal, time reopening, and verify the removed assembly clears the full opening with loose parts recoverable.
assumptions: The unspecified rim geometry provides non-damaging removable bearing engagement.
Rubber pads and stops can avoid trapping or abrading the seal.

openings.claim: The twelve-trial allowance supports one fully cycled candidate; splitting it evenly between two configurations cannot establish ten opening cycles for either.
openings.delta: Reserve the closure budget before fabrication and prioritize one configuration, with the disturbed final closure and any initial closure explicitly counted.
openings.prediction: A schedule of one initial closure, ten reopen/reclose cycles, and one spare trial uses at most twelve closure/pull trials; the tenth reclosure can be disturbed. A six-trial-per-configuration split leaves the repeated-cycle outcome untested.
openings.probe: Number the initial trial and ten cycles in advance. Apply the card at final reclosure; record position, 20 N response, reopening time and visible seal condition. Count all closure/pull trials and record fabrication/observation elapsed time.
assumptions: Ten cycles mean ten opening-and-reclosure events; initial closure consumes a trial.
One configuration is permitted by the stated maximum of two.

artifact.assessment: These are conditional design and test-budget concerns from supplied stipulations, not observed performance. Rim engagement remains unspecified; neither joint efficacy nor compliance is established.

openings.claim: Repeatable closure may require detachable padded strip stops to carry sideways load, while straps supply only the closing tension needed for seating.
openings.delta: Separates lateral registration from separation retention and seal compression, addressing the stipulated opposite-corner lift.
openings.prediction: After ten opening cycles, positive registration with low closing tension will meet the 1 mm position and 20 N pull requirements without new visible seal tears; tighter compression alone may reproduce rocking.
openings.probe: Share twelve closure/pull trials: two on a strap-only comparator, then ten on the stop-located candidate. Make each configuration final trial disturbed. Record position, pull response and corner lift.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits supplied strips, bolts and pads to form removable stops without permanent deformation or obstructing the opened aperture.

openings.claim: Can the same joint tolerate the right-contact card while preserving quick access, component recovery and seal integrity?
openings.delta: Makes disturbed serviceability an acceptance condition; the centered contact mark does not establish it.
openings.prediction: A successful candidate will still meet position, pull and 30-second reopening limits on its tenth, disturbed closure. If tilt disengages registration or requires damaging preload, it will fail those limits or the tear check.
openings.probe: Use the shared trials. Following each final disturbed pull, time one technician reopening, check the full marked opening is clear, account for loose parts and inspect the seal for new visible tears.
assumptions: Manual release and recoverable cord restraint can be arranged using supplied resources; this remains unverified.

artifact.assessment: Decision-changing uncertainties are removable stop attachment and disturbance-induced tilt. Fabricate only supplied strips; retain hatch, rim and seal. No efficacy or observed result is claimed. No assigned prior cards require lineage.

openings.claim: Padded removable strip stops could resist sideways movement while straps provide minimal seating preload, avoiding the asymmetric compression implicated in opposite-corner lift.
openings.delta: Separate lateral registration from separation restraint instead of treating tighter seal compression as sufficient retention.
openings.prediction: If reversible stop attachment is feasible, ten closures including the right-contact card closure will retain position within 1 mm during and after 20 N, reopen within 30 seconds, and leave no new visible seal tears.
openings.probe: First check reversible attachment and full opening clearance. Fabricate only with supplied resources. Use ten closure/pull trials, disturbing the tenth. Record marked displacement before, during and after pull, corner lift, reopening time and seal condition. Any outcome failure defeats this configuration; continuous disturbed seal contact is exempt.
assumptions: Existing rim geometry permits removable padded stops and strap attachment without permanent modification.
Supplied strip, bolt and strap dimensions accommodate that attachment.

openings.claim: A friction-dependent closure may appear centered after unloading while exceeding the position tolerance under load, particularly with the disturbed contact.
openings.delta: Distinguish loaded movement from residual drift; a contact mark or unloaded position cannot establish resistance to the specified pull.
openings.prediction: A feasible strap-only comparator will show greater loaded displacement than residual displacement, with the right-contact card potentially worsening the difference.
openings.probe: Allocate the remaining two permitted closure/pull trials to the comparator, one centered and one disturbed. Measure before, during and after the same 20 N pull. No loaded/residual difference defeats the prediction; passing two trials does not establish ten-cycle success. Abort any attachment that violates constraints.
assumptions: A reversible strap-only comparator can be assembled from supplied resources.

artifact.assessment: These are untested hypotheses. Twelve shared pull trials cover two configurations and both disturbances; only the stop configuration receives ten-cycle qualification. If reversible attachments are infeasible, no construction opening is supported. Stipulated observations establish neither efficacy nor attachment geometry.
